customManagers.description: The Rust toolchain pinned in every workflow (`toolchain: <X.Y.Z>`, matching devbox.json's rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt and Cargo.toml's workspace `rust-version`). Issue #1478: its datasource is `devbox`, package `rustc` — the same entry devbox.json's rustc is read from — NOT `github-releases` for rust-lang/rust. github-releases offers a Rust release the day it ships, while nixhub indexes it weeks later (measured 2026-10-02: 1.95.0 about 10 weeks after release, 1.97.0 after 2, 1.97.1 after 6), so devbox.json could not follow and scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh failed every such PR (#1470 at 1.99.0). Reading every copy from the devbox datasource is what makes grouping them sound — the objection the `Devbox toolchain packages` rule records against grouping is that two datasources offer different versions — so the `Rust toolchain (devbox, workflows and rust-version)` rule groups this pin with devbox.json's four Rust packages and with the Cargo.toml manager below, and a version is offered only once devbox can install it. The literal version is deliberately NOT written here — see the cargo-nextest manager below, where a version quoted in prose is exactly what rotted (issue #648). dtolnay/rust-toolchain publishes toolchain versions as BRANCHES with only a `v1` tag, so pinning the ref instead (`@<X.Y.Z>`) would be a version Renovate could never bump; the action stays at `@v1` and the toolchain rides an input, which splits the two concerns — the github-actions rule bumps the action, this manager bumps the toolchain. Without it the pin would silently rot, which is the failure mode that made floating `@stable` attractive in the first place. THE SECOND LANE. Renovate's github-actions manager carries a registry of actions whose version lives in an INPUT rather than the ref (`lib/modules/manager/github-actions/known-actions/rust-version.ts` in Renovate 44), and `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is in it: it reads the same `toolchain:` string and emits it as depName `rust`, depType `uses-with`, datasource `rust-version` — another day-of-release source. That lane once rode the automerging `GitHub Actions` group (PR #623 proposed the same 1.97.1 -> 1.98.0 diff as this manager's #624, with automerge on, and only an unrelated red CI stopped it), and from issue #648 until #1478 it was kept on, held for a human, as a deliberate second detector. Since #1478 it is disabled for `rust` by the `uses-with` rule near the end of packageRules, for the reason #1319 disabled it for pnpm: it reads a datasource devbox lags, so every PR it opens is one the lockstep guard rejects (#1469 was that lane's copy of #1470). What guards against silent rot instead is scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh, which fails any workflow `toolchain:` site this regex cannot read, and `renovate_reads_exactly_the_toolchain_sites_the_guard_finds` in xtask/linkage-check/src/pin_lockstep.rs, which runs this matchString over the real workflows and requires exactly the sites and versions the guard reads.

Cargo.toml's `[workspace.package] rust-version` (issue #1478). It is deliberately the toolchain this project tests, so it equals the workflow and devbox pins: `the_declared_msrv_matches_the_pinned_toolchain` in xtask/linkage-check/src/pin_lockstep.rs fails the build when it does not, and docs/develop/versioning.md says why. Renovate's cargo manager does not extract `rust-version` (checked against Renovate 44.132.2's cargo manager, 2026-10-02), so without this manager a grouped Rust PR would move devbox.json and the workflows and leave this line behind, failing that test. Same datasource and package as the workflow toolchain manager above — devbox, `rustc` — so the `Rust toolchain (devbox, workflows and rust-version)` group offers both the same version. Only the root manifest is matched, and only a quoted X.Y.Z after `rust-version =`: every member inherits the value through `rust-version.workspace = true`, which carries no version of its own and is not matched. `renovate_reads_exactly_the_declared_msrv` in pin_lockstep.rs requires this manager to extract exactly one site in the real Cargo.toml, carrying the value that test reads.

The cargo-nextest version pinned in every workflow (`tool: cargo-nextest@<X.Y.Z>`, matching devbox.json). The literal version is deliberately NOT written here, matching the convention ci.yml's own header states: a version quoted in prose rots on the next bump with nothing to catch it, and this description had been claiming 0.9.140 for the eleven days devbox.json spent on 0.9.143 (issue #648). Read the value off devbox.json. Same reasoning as the toolchain manager above: taiki-e/install-action is pinned at `@v2` and the tool version rides an input. `taiki-e/install-action` is NOT in Renovate's community-actions registry today (checked 2026-08-21), so this manager is currently the only lane that sees the pin — but that is exactly what was true of `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` until it was added, so the claim is written as an expiry date rather than a property. The `uses-with` rule below holds this pin the day the registry grows an entry for it, WITHOUT anyone having to notice.

The pnpm version pinned in every workflow (`pnpm/action-setup`'s `with: version: <X.Y.Z>`, matching devbox.json's pnpm). Issue #1319: its datasource is `devbox`, the SAME one devbox.json's pnpm is read from, NOT npm. The github-actions manager's known-actions registry also extracts this pin, as depType `uses-with` sourced from npm, and that lane is disabled below for pnpm. Reading both halves from one datasource is what makes grouping them sound: the objection the `Devbox toolchain packages` rule records against grouping is that two datasources offer different versions, and one datasource cannot. The regex expects the `uses:` line, then `with:`, then `version:` on consecutive lines, which is how every pnpm/action-setup step in .github/workflows/ is written today; a step written differently would simply not be extracted, so scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh fails any pnpm/action-setup step outside this layout (a quoted version, a flow-style `with:`, another input before `version:`), and `renovate_reads_exactly_the_pnpm_sites_the_guard_finds` in xtask/linkage-check/src/pin_lockstep.rs runs this matchString over the real workflows and requires exactly the sites and versions the guard reads.

The tauri-driver version the desktop-driver job installs (issue #953), written once as `TAURI_DRIVER_VERSION: <X.Y.Z>` in that job's `env:`. It is not duplicated in devbox.json — CI installs it with `cargo install --locked` from crates.io and devbox carries no copy — so scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh has no second site to compare it with; `desktop/scripts/driver-test.sh` reads this same line for a local run rather than restating the number, which is what keeps local and CI on one driver. No automerge rule matches it, so a bump waits for a human, which is right for the component that decides whether the flake-prone tier can even start a session.

packageRules.description: Patch bumps are in-range for Cargo and gated on CI (build + build-macos + build-windows + fast test tier).

Minor bumps automerge on green CI — but only for crates already at 1.0 or later, where a minor is genuinely backwards-compatible under semver. This is the `matchCurrentVersion` the earlier note here recommended, applied 2026-07-30 after an automerge-eligible portable-pty 0.8 -> 0.9 landed PSUEDOCONSOLE_INHERIT_CURSOR and stalled every Windows pane. 0.x minors are handled by the next rule.

A 0.x minor is a BREAKING change as far as Cargo is concerned (0.8 -> 0.9 is not compatible), so it is a major in everything but Renovate's label. Held for a human, matching the intent 'automerge anything that is not a major'. Stated as its own rule rather than left to the default so the intent is explicit and labelled: portable-pty 0.9.0 reached main through exactly this gap.

Renovate ignores this crate entirely: no PRs, and no Dependency Dashboard entry to remember to check. portable-pty is held at =0.8.1 deliberately (see the Cargo.toml comment): 0.9.0 sets PSUEDOCONSOLE_INHERIT_CURSOR, so ConPTY withholds a Windows pane's output until a terminal answers ESC[6n, stalling every pane. Renovate re-proposed 0.9.0 within minutes of the v0.35.1 release; a standing PR for a pin held on purpose is pure noise, and the unpin is gated on a PRODUCT decision (native Windows support), not on a version becoming available — so no dependency bot can know when the time is right. Safe to silence because the `security` CI job runs `cargo audit` on every PR and every push to main, so a vulnerability in this crate surfaces there regardless of Renovate. The reminder to revisit lives in the Cargo.toml comment and the tracking issue, i.e. where the Windows decision will actually be made.

Ordinary devbox packages automerge on green CI. Note what green means for one of these PRs: ci.yml's `changes` gate skips all four required jobs when a Renovate PR touches nothing but devbox.json/devbox.lock, and GitHub counts a skipped required check as passing, so the only check that has actually LOOKED at the change is the `devbox` job. That is acceptable for vals/gh/jq/ffmpeg, which nothing else in the repository pins. It is not acceptable for the six toolchain packages, which the next rule takes out of this group.

Devbox toolchain packages, held for the SAME human who holds the workflow pins below. These six are the devbox half of a version pinned TWICE: `.github/workflows/` carries the other half (`toolchain:` for the four Rust components, `tool: cargo-nextest@` for nextest, `pnpm/action-setup`'s `version:` for pnpm), and the two halves have to move as one change, because `cargo test-fast` in a devbox shell and `cargo nextest run` in CI are the same claim only while they agree. Issue #648: until this rule existed the two halves had OPPOSITE automerge policies — this group merged itself unattended while the `custom.regex` rule below held the workflow half for a human — so they separated on every release BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by anyone forgetting. cargo-nextest reached 0.9.143 in devbox.json via automerged #510 on 2026-08-11 and ci.yml sat on 0.9.140 for eleven days, invisible until somebody diffed the two files. Removing the asymmetry is the fix. GROUPING THE TWO LANES WAS THE OTHER OPTION AND IS WORSE WHILE THE TWO HALVES READ DIFFERENT DATASOURCES: a shared `groupName` bundles the two PRs when both lanes have an update, but it cannot make the lanes OFFER the same version, and they routinely do not — the devbox datasource is nixpkgs, which never carried nextest 0.9.141 or 0.9.142 (both published to crates.io the same afternoon as 0.9.143) and had no Rust 1.98.0 when this was written (2026-08-22), which is why #647 was held open. So the common case is one lane holding an upgrade the other cannot match, and the grouped PR then contains exactly one half — the same drift, now wearing a title that says lockstep — while a group spanning `automerge: true` and `automerge: false` would have to be resolved by dropping automerge here anyway. Reading BOTH halves from the devbox datasource removes that objection, and it is what issue #1319 did for pnpm and issue #1478 for the Rust toolchain; cargo-nextest's workflow half still reads crates.io, so the objection stands for it. WHAT THIS COSTS, for cargo-nextest: two PRs per release that somebody must click, where the devbox one used to be free. The frequency is low (nextest roughly monthly, nixpkgs lagging it), and the click is not `read a diff` but `put the other half in this branch and merge once`, which is the work the lockstep requires however it is scheduled. It also does NOT gate anything by itself: a devbox-only PR skips all four required checks (see the rule above), so this is a label plus a human. `scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh` is the part with teeth — the `devbox` job, the only ungated one, runs it, and `cargo test-fast` runs it via xtask/linkage-check. Naming six packages is an enumeration, which #641 argued against for the depType whitelist; it is a different thing here — not a blacklist of names caught misbehaving, but the closed set of devbox packages duplicated into `.github/workflows/`. If that set grows and this list does not follow, the guard still catches the drift, so the enforcement does not depend on this rule being complete. It grew on 2026-09-24 (issue #1262), when `pnpm` joined. Its workflow half used to arrive through the github-actions manager's known-actions registry as depType `uses-with` (the lane #911 took it to v12 by), sourced from npm, which offered versions nixpkgs did not carry and so produced PRs the lockstep guard had to reject (#1317, #1318). Since issue #1319 that lane is disabled for pnpm and a `custom.regex` manager reads the workflow half from the devbox datasource instead; the `pnpm (devbox and workflows)` rule near the end of this list groups the two halves, overriding the `groupName: null` this entry sets. Issue #1478 did the same for rustc, cargo, clippy and rustfmt: the workflows' `toolchain:` pins and Cargo.toml's `rust-version` are read from the devbox datasource (package `rustc`), the github-actions `uses-with` lane is disabled for `rust`, and the `Rust toolchain (devbox, workflows and rust-version)` rule near the end of this list groups all of them, overriding this entry's `groupName: null` too. So of the six packages named here, only cargo-nextest gets its devbox half as a PR of its own.

Lock file maintenance is disabled for devbox.lock, because Renovate resolves the lock inside its own throwaway container and devbox writes an ABSOLUTE path for `path:` flake entries. PR #348 therefore added a `path:gcloud#google-cloud-sdk` entry whose `resolved` field pointed at `path:/tmp/renovate/repos/github/vfarcic/dot-agent-deck/gcloud`, a directory that exists on no real machine; 77b5e87 removed it. The entry is not something devbox recreates — `devbox install` leaves the lock at 17 entries and resolves the local flake from devbox.json — so it is purely an artifact of where the bot ran, and every lock file maintenance run would re-add it. Actual devbox package bumps are unaffected: they still flow through the `Devbox packages` rule above, so only the wholesale lock refresh stops. Consequence to accept: the nixpkgs revisions pinned in devbox.lock now only move when a package bump moves them, so refresh them by hand (`devbox update`) if they drift too far.

Automerge covers ACTION REFS ONLY — `uses: owner/repo@ref`, which is depType `action`. This is a WHITELIST on purpose, and `matchDepTypes` is the load-bearing line in it. The github-actions manager emits six depTypes (`action`, `docker`, `container`, `service`, `github-runner`, `uses-with`), and this rule used to match the manager with no depType filter at all, so it automerged every one of them — including tool versions read out of an action's INPUTS. That is how the Rust toolchain pin acquired an automerging lane (see the customManager description above and the `uses-with` rule below). Whitelisting rather than excluding the one dep name observed misbehaving is the point: Renovate's input-detection registry is a list that GROWS, so a blacklist is only ever correct until the next release, whereas anything this manager learns to detect tomorrow falls OUTSIDE this rule and is held by default. The cost of being wrong in this direction is a PR someone has to click; in the other direction it is an unreviewed toolchain change on main.

Everything the github-actions manager extracts that is NOT an action ref is held for a human and labelled. Stated as its own rule rather than left to Renovate's automerge default, matching the convention of the 0.x-minor rule above: a hold that exists only as an absence is invisible on the PR page and impossible to grep for. `uses-with` is the one that matters here — it is a version string embedded in an action's inputs, which in this repo's workflows has meant the Rust toolchain (`dtolnay/rust-toolchain`'s `toolchain:`), pnpm (`pnpm/action-setup`'s `version:`) and the desktop jobs' Node (`actions/setup-node`'s `node-version:`), i.e. TOOLCHAINS wearing a GitHub Actions costume. Two of those are now switched off in this lane altogether, by rules near the end of this list — pnpm by issue #1319 and the Rust toolchain by issue #1478 — because the lane read them from datasources devbox lags, and custom.regex managers read them from the devbox datasource instead. So today this hold governs Node, and whatever the registry learns to read next. A toolchain bump is not an action bump: it changes what compiles, it is where new deny-by-default rustc lints and clippy lints arrive, and in this repo it must move in lockstep with devbox.json by hand. Worse, before this rule the toolchain rode the `GitHub Actions` GROUP, so a Rust bump could arrive bundled inside a PR titled 'update GitHub Actions' alongside a handful of ordinary `@v7` bumps and automerge without ever being read on its own. The remaining depTypes (container/service/docker images, `runs-on:` runner versions) are listed for completeness — this repo has none today, and if it grows one, a base image or runner change is also not something to land unread.

The gh-aw `*.lock.yml` files are GENERATED by `gh aw compile`, and Renovate cannot produce a correct bump for one. It rewrites `uses: owner/repo@<sha> # <version>` lines like any other workflow, but each lock also carries a `gh-aw-manifest` comment recording the SHA and version of every action it pins, plus a generated body compiled against that version. Renovate updates the first and not the rest, so EVERY PR it opens against these paths is internally inconsistent by construction — not occasionally, structurally. MEASURED, three times in two days: #989 bumped `github/gh-aw-actions/setup` v0.86.2 -> v0.89.0 in `pr-review.lock.yml`, rewrote all six `uses:` lines consistently, left the manifest at v0.86.2, merged through Renovate's ruleset bypass with nothing to stop it, and every agent job then died with `Gateway configuration must specify exactly one of 'agentId' or 'agentIds'` — the v0.89.0 action being handed config generated by the v0.86.2 compiler. #996 reverted it by recompiling at v0.86.2 and added `xtask/linkage-check/src/gh_aw_lock_consistency.rs` to catch the next one. The next two arrived immediately: #987 (v0.86.3) and #997 (v0.89.0 again, the known-bad version), both red on that guard across `build`, `build-macos`, `build-windows` and `e2e-deterministic`. Closing them individually does not help, because a close rejects one VERSION and the next release re-offers. WHAT THIS COSTS, stated plainly: no PR and no Dependency Dashboard entry when gh-aw releases, so nobody is told. That is a smaller loss than it looks, because Renovate was never watching the thing that decides these files — the `gh aw` CLI version, which nothing in `devbox.json` or `scripts/` pins, so the upgrade path was always a human running `gh aw compile <workflow-name>` (never bare; a bare compile rewrites GH_AW_ACTION_FAILURE_ISSUE_EXPIRES_HOURS to "0" in every lock) at a version they chose. Scoped as a packageRule rather than top-level `ignorePaths` on purpose: `ignorePaths` is unset here, so it carries Renovate's defaults (`**/node_modules/**`, `**/tests/**`, `**/vendor/**` and the rest), and setting it would REPLACE them — silently re-enabling scanning of this repo's own `tests/` and the desktop/site `node_modules`. The guard in `gh_aw_lock_consistency.rs` stays regardless: it is what catches a hand-edit, a future bot, or this rule being removed.

The toolchain pins read by custom.regex managers are held for a human even on a patch: the Rust toolchain (depName `rustc`, which covers the workflows' `toolchain:` and Cargo.toml's `rust-version`) and the workflows' cargo-nextest. They must stay in lockstep with devbox.json's rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt and cargo-nextest pins — that lockstep is the whole point of pinning them. For the Rust toolchain the devbox half arrives in the same PR, grouped by the `Rust toolchain (devbox, workflows and rust-version)` rule (issue #1478); for cargo-nextest, whose workflow half is read from crates.io, the matching devbox bump is a separate PR that has to be brought into this branch. A Rust patch release is also exactly where a new clippy lint appears, which is a `-D warnings` failure to read rather than automerge. Corrected 2026-08-22 (issue #648): this description used to add `and nothing enforces it automatically`, and that sentence turned out to be a prediction rather than a caveat — the devbox half was automerging while this half waited, and cargo-nextest drifted 0.9.143/0.9.140 for eleven days. Two things changed. The devbox half is now held by the `Devbox toolchain packages` rule above, so both halves wait for the same person and land together. And the lockstep IS enforced automatically now: `scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh` compares the two files and fails, from `cargo test-fast` (so the three required build jobs and a contributor's local gate) and from ci.yml's `devbox` job (the one job no `changes` gate can skip). Landing this lane alone therefore turns the PR red rather than main. This rule is ALSO not the only hold on these pins and must not be read as one: the same `toolchain:` string is seen by the github-actions manager under depName `rust`, which the `uses-with` rule near the end of this list disables (issue #1478), and the depType rules above are what hold any lane the registry adds later. Keep all of it — this one says WHY the pin is held, those say WHERE ELSE it can be reached from, and the guard is what notices when a hold is bypassed anyway.

Do not propose an npm package until it is three days old. pnpm 11 (arrived via #776) enforces a supply-chain policy that REJECTS lockfile entries for packages published within the last 24 hours — its own default, not configured here — so a PR opened hours after publication fails `desktop-web` at `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION, and one that MERGES leaves `main` red until the package ages out (issue #813). Measured twice in two days: lucide-react 1.38.0 merged via #790 and held `main` red ~16h, and 1.39.0 arrived on #809 at 1h28m old. The failure is time-based and self-healing, which is what makes it corrosive rather than merely annoying — a recurring red check that means nothing trains everyone to ignore red checks, and an unrelated PR opened in that window inherits it (#805 failed at 23h31m, 29 minutes short). Renovate's internalChecksFilter holds the update rather than opening a PR, so nothing is created for CI to reject. THREE days rather than 24 hours on purpose: pnpm evaluates the cutoff at install time, so matching the figure exactly leaves no margin for a PR opened at the boundary, and for the packages this actually affects — an icon set or test tooling — three days costs nothing. SCOPED TO npm DELIBERATELY: pnpm's policy governs npm packages only, so cargo, devbox and github-actions lanes keep their current cadence; a global delay would change three lanes to fix a problem in one. NOTE the 24-hour figure is pnpm's default, not a value pinned in this repository — if it changes, or is later configured explicitly, this number has to track it, which is a two-halves-of-one-number problem of the same shape as #648 in a lane scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh does not cover. What bounds it since issue #1262 is that pnpm itself is pinned to an exact version in devbox.json and the workflows, and that guard holds the two together, so the default can move only in a pnpm bump somebody reviews — before #1262 CI took `version: 12`, i.e. any 12.x the day it shipped. It was deliberately NOT pinned as an explicit `minimumReleaseAge` in desktop/pnpm-workspace.yaml: pnpm 11.22.0 makes `minimumReleaseAgeStrict` default to true once `minimumReleaseAge` is set explicitly (its changelog dates that to 11.0.4), while the built-in 1440-minute default stays non-strict, so writing down the same number would change behaviour rather than record it.

Hold the Tauri CRATES one day longer than the npm lane above (four days against three), and never automerge them, so a Rust-only half of `config:recommended`'s tauri monorepo group cannot land by itself. Equal delays would not be enough: Renovate counts each registry's release age from that registry's own publish time, so if crates.io publishes before npm, an equal age makes the crates eligible first (Qodo and Greptile on PR #1363). The extra day covers a same-day publish; `automerge: false` overrides the cargo minor-update automerge rule above for these crates, so anything that still splits waits for a person instead of merging. Without this they split: the npm rule above holds `@tauri-apps/api` and `@tauri-apps/cli` while the cargo lane has no delay, so Renovate opened #1358 with the Rust half alone (tauri 2.11.6 → 2.12.0, tauri-build 2.6.3 → 2.7.0, Cargo.lock only) the same day both halves were published, and it merged. `tauri build` refuses a crate and an npm package on different major/minor releases ("Found version mismatched Tauri packages"), so `main` then failed the desktop-driver job and would have failed release.yml's desktop-bundle leg, which runs the same build; the npm half could follow only through a temporary, owner-approved `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` in desktop/pnpm-workspace.yaml (#1360), because pnpm's 24-hour release-age gate (the rule above) otherwise refused packages that young. This is the exception to the npm rule's 'SCOPED TO npm DELIBERATELY', and it is scoped to the Tauri crates alone for the same reason: the rest of the cargo lane keeps its cadence.

Deliberate EXACT pins in Cargo.toml, never automerged. crossterm's pin is load-bearing: `ui::ctrl_c0_byte` documents crossterm 0.28.1's decoder behaviour and `keyevent_ctrl_c0_matches_crossterm_decoder` guards it (PRD #227). See also #242 (crossterm 0.28.1 + 0.29.0 coexist because ratatui 0.30 pulls 0.29 via ratatui-crossterm). portable-pty is pinned at =0.8.1 because 0.9.0 sets PSUEDOCONSOLE_INHERIT_CURSOR, which makes ConPTY withhold a Windows pane's output until a terminal answers ESC[6n — see the Cargo.toml comment. WITHOUT this entry a 0.8 -> 0.9 bump counts as a `minor` for the cargo rule above and would AUTOMERGE, silently reintroducing the stall; that is how 0.9.0 landed the first time.
Major bumps always stay manual.

Issue #1319: the npm-sourced lane for pnpm/action-setup's `version:` is off. It proposed pnpm releases nixpkgs had not packaged yet, so devbox.json could not follow and scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh failed every such PR (#1317 at 11.28.0, #1318 at 12). The workflow pin is read by the `custom.regex` pnpm manager instead, from the devbox datasource.

Issue #1319: devbox.json's pnpm and the workflows' pnpm/action-setup `version:` move in ONE PR. Both are read from the devbox datasource, so a version is offered only once nixhub carries it, and both halves are offered the same version. The PR therefore passes scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh by construction, and its arrival is the signal that a newer pnpm is usable. Held for a human like the rest of the toolchain pins. Placed after the `Devbox toolchain packages` rule so its groupName overrides that rule's `groupName: null`, and before the release.yml artifact-actions hold, which the release-workflow wiring guard requires to stay the last rule.

Issue #1478: the rust-version-sourced lane for dtolnay/rust-toolchain's `toolchain:` input is off, as #1319 turned the npm-sourced one off for pnpm. Renovate's `rust-version` datasource carries a Rust release the day it ships while nixhub indexes it weeks later, so devbox.json could not follow and scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh failed every PR this lane opened (#1469 at 1.99.0). The workflow pin is read by the `custom.regex` toolchain manager instead, from the devbox datasource. `rust` is the depName this lane gives dtolnay/rust-toolchain's input (measured with Renovate 44.132.2 in dry run, 2026-10-02), and in that version's known-actions registry the other two Rust actions it reads, moonrepo/setup-rust and actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain, name the same package, so a job switching to one of them should stay off this lane too.

Issue #1478: the Rust toolchain moves in ONE PR — devbox.json's rustc, cargo, clippy and rustfmt, every workflow `toolchain:` pin, and Cargo.toml's workspace `rust-version`. All of them are read from the devbox datasource, so a version is offered only once nixhub carries it. The workflow and rust-version sites read package `rustc`; the four devbox packages each read their own nixhub entry, and those four carried identical version lists when checked on 2026-10-02. If they ever diverge (clippy indexed at a release rustc is not, say), the grouped PR carries a subset and scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh fails it, which is the safe direction: it then waits for the lagging package rather than pinning one devbox cannot install. Because the PR touches Cargo.toml and the workflows as well as devbox.json, ci.yml's `changes` gate does not classify it as devbox-only, so the required build jobs run on it. Held for a human like the rest of the toolchain pins: a toolchain bump is where new deny-by-default rustc lints and clippy lints arrive. Placed after the `Devbox toolchain packages` rule so its groupName overrides that rule's `groupName: null`, and before the release.yml artifact-actions hold, which the release-workflow wiring guard requires to stay the last rule.

The weekly lock file maintenance PR automerges, and only through Renovate's OWN merge (`platformAutomerge: false`), which waits for every check on the head to be green instead of only the five the ruleset requires. WHY IT NEVER LANDED BEFORE: the `npm` rule above gives this update its three-day `minimumReleaseAge`, but a lock file refresh carries no `releaseTimestamp` — Renovate deletes the lock and hands the whole resolution to the package manager, and its docs list `lockFileMaintenance` as an update type `minimumReleaseAge` cannot apply to. Under the default `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-required` a missing timestamp counts as not yet aged, so `renovate/stability-days` was pending permanently, not until a package aged out: it was pending on all 12 heads of `renovate/lock-file-maintenance` that CI ran after the three-day rule landed (#814) and success on none, across #1070, #1208 and #1377, and #1208 was then merged by hand inside a 'window' that could never close (#1222). Renovate does re-evaluate it on each run that processes the branch; it posts a new status only when the verdict changes, which is why #1377's sat unchanged for ~42 hours. `timestamp-optional` is scoped to this update type, so the npm and Tauri rules judge ordinary updates exactly as before, and `minimumReleaseAge` itself is left alone because Renovate derives npm's `--before` cutoff (pi-extension/package-lock.json) from it. WHAT HOLDS THE 24-HOUR FLOOR INSTEAD is pnpm, at resolution: Renovate runs `pnpm install --lockfile-only` with the highest stable pnpm matching `>=9`, which it derives from `lockfileVersion: '9.0'` because desktop/package.json names no `packageManager` — a 12.x on 2026-10-02, not the 11.22.0 devbox.json pins — and both 11.22.0 and 12.8.1 default `minimumReleaseAge` to 1440 minutes and pick the newest version at least that old. That default is non-strict, so where NO mature version satisfies a range pnpm takes an immature one and writes it to pnpm-workspace.yaml's `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`, a file Renovate does not commit; that lock reaches CI with an entry `desktop-web`'s frozen install rejects. WHY `platformAutomerge: false` IS LOAD-BEARING: `desktop-web` is not a required check and GitHub's auto-merge waits only for required ones, so platform automerge could land exactly that lock and turn `main` red (#813). Cargo is the same shape with no floor at all: Cargo.lock is refreshed by a bare `cargo update`, and the Tauri crates' four-day rule cannot match an update that has no package name, so a refresh can pair a tauri crate published minutes earlier with the older npm half — which `desktop-driver`, also unrequired, rejects ('Found version mismatched Tauri packages'). Renovate's own merge counts every check run and commit status, required or not, reads queued, cancelled or timed-out runs as not green, and never merges in the same run that pushed the commit. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: it merges under the `pull_request`-mode ruleset bypass like every other automerge group here, so no approval is involved (docs/develop/governance.md, 'Renovate and automerge'); a red lock stays red until Renovate next regenerates the branch, because nothing automatic re-runs CI on it; and devbox.lock stays out, as the rule above disables its maintenance. The Monday schedule is kept: it governs when the refresh is cut, not when it may merge.

The two artifact actions in release.yml are held for a human even on a digest, pin, patch or minor update, overriding the automerging `GitHub Actions` rule above. WHY: `desktop-sign` (PRD #757) is the one job that holds the Apple Developer ID private key, and it runs `actions/download-artifact` and `actions/upload-artifact` — the download before anything else, where it can change what every later step executes (through `$GITHUB_PATH` or `$GITHUB_ENV`, for instance), and the upload while the throwaway keychain holding that key and `AuthKey.p8` are still on the runner. Those two actions are the only third-party code in that job; everything else is its own inline steps and the macOS runner's system tools. An automerged digest bump is a change to code that runs next to the key, landed with no human reading it, which is exactly what the job was split out of `desktop-bundle` to avoid. `matchFileNames` scopes it to release.yml, so these actions keep automerging in every other workflow; within release.yml it also holds every other job's uses of the same two actions, because the rule matches by file rather than by job, and holding a few extra PRs is the cheap direction to be wrong in. `groupName: null` takes these updates out of the `GitHub Actions` group, so they get their own PR rather than riding a grouped, automerged one — the same shape as the `Devbox toolchain packages` rule. It is LAST in the list on purpose: later packageRules override earlier ones, so nothing below can hand these back to the group. BEFORE MERGING one of these PRs, verify the new digest is the commit the release tag names in the action's own repository (`gh api repos/actions/upload-artifact/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`, which dereferences an annotated tag), and read the diff between the old and new digest. docs/develop/desktop-signing.md, 'Dependency updates on the signing runner'. If `desktop-sign` gains another action, add it here.
